title: Human Dignity
definition: Human dignity is the God-given worth of every person because human beings are created in God's image.
summary: Every person has value because God created humanity in His image.
christFocus: Jesus demonstrated human dignity by entering human life, caring for the weak, and giving Himself to redeem sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Human dignity does not come from usefulness, independence, strength, intelligence, wealth, or social approval. It comes from God, who made human beings in His image.

Because every person has dignity, people must not be treated as disposable, invisible, or beyond care. Scripture calls God's people to protect life, speak truthfully, show compassion, and honor others.

The Gospel deepens this doctrine. Christ took on true humanity and died for sinners, showing both the seriousness of sin and the worth of people made by God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people feel worthless because of disability, addiction, poverty, trauma, age, failure, or rejection. Human dignity matters because it declares that worth is received from God, not earned by performance.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor people with your words, attention, service, and protection. Refuse contempt. Ask God to help you see others as He sees them and to defend the vulnerable with truth and compassion.
